content.title: About
content.content: Apricot is a juicy fruit of the apricot tree (Prunus armeniaca) that grows in temperate regions. The fruit has a soft, mildly sweet‑tart flesh covered by a thin edible skin. It is eaten fresh and also used in cooking, desserts, jams, compotes, and dried fruit preparations.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Apricot belongs to the Rosaceae family and is closely related to peaches, plums, and cherries.
High in β‑carotene, apricots are an excellent source of provitamin A.
Cultivation dates back to ancient China, Persia, and the Mediterranean basin.
Dried apricots can contain up to 4 g of sugar per 100 g.
Apricot blossoms appear early in spring, often before the leaves.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C enhances antioxidant protection and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Low‑calorie fruit
items.content: Apricots are suitable for weight‑management diets due to their low fat and moderate calorie content.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to apricots.

items.title: Cyanogenic glycosides in the pit
items.content: Apricot pits contain amygdalin, which can release cyanide when processed; they should not be eaten.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Natural sugars may be a concern for people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fresh apricots are enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, cereals, and baked goods. They can be baked, made into jams, compotes, or dried. The skin is usually left on because it is edible and fiber‑rich.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store apricots in the refrigerator in a plastic container or bag to prevent drying out. For longer storage, freeze sliced pieces. Use fruits that are soft, free of spots, and show no signs of spoilage.
